questions.question: Why must large food molecules like proteins and carbohydrates be digested in the human body?
options: To turn them into vitamins
To break them down into smaller molecules that can be absorbed
To make them taste better
To convert them directly into carbon dioxide gas

questions.question: Once nutrients are absorbed from our food, how do they reach the cells in our body where they are needed?
options: They are carried by the nervous system
They are pumped through the lymphatic system only
They are transported by the blood around the body
They float through air pockets in the muscles

questions.question: How do some very small nutrient molecules move from the digestive system into the blood?
options: By the process of diffusion
By being squeezed through tiny valves
By active evaporation
By dissolving into the bones first

questions.question: Which of these features of the small intestine lining helps to increase the amount of absorption?
options: A smooth, thick layer of protective wax
A large surface area provided by many tiny folds and villi
A very cold temperature to slow down movement
A hard, muscular shell that grinds food

questions.question: What is a bacterium, such as those found in our digestive system?
options: A multi-cellular animal with a simple heart
A tiny plant that uses sunlight to make food
A microscopic organism consisting of a single living cell
A non-living chemical crystal

questions.question: Which statement is true about all the bacteria found in the world?
options: All bacteria cause harmful diseases and must be destroyed
Some bacteria cause disease, but many are harmless and some are helpful
Bacteria only exist inside the human stomach and nowhere else
Bacteria are all helpful and none can cause diseases

questions.question: Where in the human body do helpful bacteria naturally live to assist with our digestive health?
options: Inside the windpipe
Inside the human digestive system
Directly inside the red blood cells
On the surface of the teeth only

questions.question: How do helpful bacteria inside our digestive system assist in digesting foods like certain plant fibres?
options: They release enzymes that digest food we cannot digest ourselves
They heat up the stomach using chemical energy
They physically chew the food with microscopic teeth
They acidify the food until it melts into gas

questions.question: How do helpful gut bacteria protect us from harmful pathogens that enter our digestive system?
options: They produce white blood cells to attack them
They compete against the pathogens for resources and space
They build physical walls around the pathogens
They absorb the pathogens into their own cells

questions.question: What is the main difference between mechanical and chemical digestion?
options: Mechanical digestion uses enzymes, while chemical digestion only uses water
Mechanical digestion physically breaks food into smaller pieces, while chemical digestion uses chemicals to break chemical bonds
Mechanical digestion only happens in the liver, while chemical digestion happens in the mouth
Mechanical digestion produces new nutrients, while chemical digestion only moves food

questions.question: Which three main groups of nutrients make up the bulk of the food we eat?
options: Vitamins, minerals, and water
Carbohydrates, proteins, and fats
Sugars, starch, and fibre only
Calcium, iron, and sodium

questions.question: What role do enzymes play in the chemical digestion of our food?
options: They slow down digestion so the body can absorb nutrients gradually
They act as biological catalysts to speed up the chemical breakdown of nutrients
They physically crush the food in the stomach
They act as hormones that control our appetite

questions.question: When enzymes digest proteins, what smaller molecules are they broken down into?
options: Fatty acids and glycerol
Starch and simple sugars
Amino acids
Carbon dioxide and water

questions.question: If you want to test a food sample to see if it contains starch, which chemical reagent should you add?
options: Biuret solution
Ethanol
Iodine solution
Benedict's solution

questions.question: Which reagent is used to test for the presence of simple sugars, which are produced when starch is broken down?
options: Benedict's solution
Iodine solution
Biuret solution
Hydrochloric acid

questions.question: A student adds Biuret reagent to a food sample, and the solution turns from blue to purple. What does this result indicate?
options: The food contains a high amount of starch
The food contains protein
The food is rich in simple sugars
The food contains fats only

questions.question: Which of the following shows the correct order in which food moves through the organs of the digestive system?
options: Mouth -> Stomach -> Small Intestine -> Large Intestine
Mouth -> Large Intestine -> Stomach -> Small Intestine
Stomach -> Mouth -> Small Intestine -> Large Intestine
Mouth -> Esophagus -> Large Intestine -> Small Intestine

questions.question: How is the stomach adapted to help break down food during digestion?
options: It has a highly alkaline environment to dissolve fats
It has muscular walls to churn food and produces acid and enzymes
It is extremely dry to absorb water quickly
It is lined with tiny hairs that filter out large food particles

questions.question: What happens to the food material that cannot be digested or absorbed by the body?
options: It is turned into urine in the kidneys
It is passed out of the body as faeces
It is breathed out through the lungs as carbon dioxide
It is stored forever in the liver

questions.question: Why does the presence of villi in the small intestine speed up the absorption of nutrients?
options: Villi make the small intestine wider so more food can fit
Villi greatly increase the surface area available for absorption
Villi cool down the food so it dissolves faster
Villi produce mucus that traps the nutrients
